{{nihongo|'''Uneotsutamoto Shrine'''|畝尾都多本神社}} is a shrine in {{ill|Kashihara, Nara|Q496319|qid=Q496319}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is located on the northwestern foot of {{ill|Mount Amanokagu|Q11443780|qid=Q11443780}}, and to the adjacent northeast stands another Shikinaisha, {{ill|Uneoza Taketsuyasugami Shrine|Q30931377|qid=Q30931377}}. It is also called "Nakisawa Shrine" (written with characters such as 啼澤, 哭沢, 泣沢) and is known as "Nakisawa no Mori." {{nihongo|'''Uneotsutamoto Shrine'''|畝尾都多本神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

== Enshrined deity ==
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nakisawa-me-no-Kami}} (なきさわめのかみ)
There is a well called Nakisawa, and that well is worshiped as the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shintai}}<ref>{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} Jinmyōchō</ref>.

== History ==
The founding is unknown, but in Book 2, poem 202 of the '{{ill|Man'yōshū|Q834321|qid=Q834321}}':
:Though sacred sake is offered and prayers made at Nakisawa Shrine, my jewel child does not know the high sun.
:(Even though sacred sake is offered to the goddess of Nakisawa Shrine and prayers are made to prolong the life of the deceased prince, the prince has finally gone to rule the heavens.)
The left-side note records:
:"This one poem, according to {{ill|Ruijū Karin|Q11665187|qid=Q11665187}}, is said to be a song by {{ill|Hinokuma no Ōkimi|Q30932401|qid=Q30932401}} lamenting {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nakisawa-me-no-Kami}}<ref>{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}</ref>. Looking at the Nihongi: in autumn, seventh month, on the day Kōjutsu, in the 10th year (696), later prince no mikoto passed away."
This is a waka of resentment toward Nakisawa-me-no-Kami: in {{ill|696|Q23486|qid=Q23486|lt=Jitō Tennō 10 (696)}}, Matsukuma no Ōkimi offered sacred sake to a revival deity and prayed for {{ill|Prince Takechi|Q837590|qid=Q837590}}'s life, but he did not return to life<ref>{{ill|Man'yōshū|Q834321|qid=Q834321}}</ref><ref>[http://www.city.kashihara.nara.jp/kankou/own_kankou/kankou/spot/uneotsutamoto.html Kashihara City / Uneotsutamoto Shrine]</ref>. From this, Uneotsutamoto Shrine is thought to have already existed in the {{ill|Asuka period|Q210688|qid=Q210688}}. On a precinct stone monument, in addition to the above Man'yōshū annotation, are engraved a passage from {{ill|Hirata Atsutane|Q2572749|qid=Q2572749}}'s 'Tamasuki' saying "Nakisawa-me deity is a deity for life-begging," and a quotation from {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|Q384647|qid=Q384647}}'s '{{ill|Kojiki-den|Q11410835|qid=Q11410835}}' saying "etymologically, sawa-me connects to rain and is a water deity"<ref>[http://engishiki.org/yamato/html/031410-01.html Uneotsutamoto Shrine - Investigation of Engishiki shrines]</ref>.

In the 1446 (Bun'an 3) 'Washū Gokōri Jinja Jinmyōchō Tairyaku Chūkai,' together with {{ill|Amanokaguyama Shrine|Q98082987|qid=Q98082987|lt=Amanokagu ni Imasu Kushimakoto Shrine}}, Sakamon Shrine (Ame-no-Iwato Shrine), and {{ill|Uneoza Taketsuyasugami Shrine|Q30931377|qid=Q30931377}}, it is referred to as "Amanokagu-yama ni Imasu Yotsudokoro Shrines"<ref>[https://genbu.net/data/yamato/tutamoto_title.htm Uneotsutamoto Shrine]</ref>.

It is identified with Uneotsutamoto Shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki-listed shrine}} and stands adjacent to the also-listed {{ill|Uneoza Taketsuyasugami Shrine|Q30931377|qid=Q30931377}}. Remains of the "Kaguyama Shōsō," an office that stored and managed {{ill|shōzei|Q11545591|qid=Q11545591}} in the {{ill|Nara period|Q189178|qid=Q189178}}, have been excavated nearby.

The shrine buildings were rebuilt in the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} era.

== Name origin ==
"Une" means a wavy/ridged place. "O" means where a mountain foot stretches long like an animal tail. "Uneo" thus means mountain foot; this refers to the foot of Mount Kagu.
